title: Staccato voices — probe notebook & request stitch
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a compact, working notebook capturing short, staccato (fragmentary) customer vignettes + synthesis about recently surfaced runtime and UX asks. Goal is: rapid translation into 2–3 low-effort probes we can run with SRE/serving-runtime next sprint. Not polished — intentionally terse.

Topline themes (quick take):
- Surprise fallbacks: customers report opaque model fallbacks mid-session (e.g., request routed to a smaller quantized variant) and no visible indicator. They lose trust (esp for safety-sensitive outputs).
- KV/cache pain: multiple customers want per-tenant control for KV cache TTL and ability to forcibly invalidate prefixes programmatically. Current all-or-nothing cache semantics cause stale completions in chat flows.
- Token budgeting + billing surprises: customers building multi-route pipelines are seeing unexpectedly high bill spikes from background reranks/embeddings that are not surfaced in per-route cost SLOs.
- Streaming fragility: reconnects during long-stream sessions frequently duplicate final tokens or drop tool-calls. Implementation variance across SDKs.
- Dedicated burst expectations: Dedicated customers want a documented and configurable burst pool separate from reserved lanes (clear semantics for throttling during spikes).

Representative vignettes (raw):
- Retail search team (large retailer): "We had a session where the model dropped knowledge in the middle — it went from long-form product reasoning to short template answers. No way to know why. Customer-facing app looked broken." (asked for per-request model variant transparency + sticky model pin for the session)
- Fintech startup: "We cache user context to speed up chat. Last week we changed prompt tokenization and old cache entries started producing hallucinated account references." (asks: cache versioning, TTL, and manual purge API)
- Enterprise legal: "Our integration sometimes triggers a rerank pipeline that explodes tokens in the background. The route shows low token spend but our bill doubled due to reranks." (asks: per-route breakdown including sub-requests)

Candidate low-effort probes (MVP experiments):
1) Probe: session-sticky model pin (2-week spike)
   - What: Add a per-session header to pin to a model family (e.g., redwood-gpt-*-v1) with a visible header in responses when fallback occurs.
   - Why: quick trust fix; surface fallbacks to clients and let them opt in to sticky sessions.
   - Risk/effort: low — routing flag + response header + SDK patch.
   - Success metric: reduction in "why did it change mid-session" tickets by 60% for participants.

2) Probe: tenant-level KV cache controls (alpha)
   - What: small control plane flag to set TTL per-tenant and an API endpoint to evict keys by prefix. Logging of evictions.
   - Why: addresses stale-context hallucination reports.
   - Risk/effort: medium — needs auth/ops guardrails and a short retention policy.
   - Rollout: opt-in for 5 pilot customers (Retail search, Fintech).

3) Probe: per-route microbilling telemetry (experimental)
   - What: emit an enriched event for each top-level request that includes token counts for child operations (reranks, embedding calls) and route-label. Expose as separate small CSV export.
   - Why: immediate visibility to customers and CS to hunt billing surprises.
   - Risk/effort: low-medium — instrumentation and small export UI/CSV.

Engineering blockers & open Qs (for sprint sync):
- Routing visibility: do we currently persist the model-variant chosen per-request in trace logs with tenant visibility? If not, minimal change needed? (ask: eng-serving-runtime)
- KV eviction auth: who owns the auth model for cache control APIs in Private deployments (CS vs infra)? Need quick doc.
- Billing schema changes: small event adds may require downstream billing pipeline review — tag finance.

Suggested owners for probes:
- Session sticky: eng-serving-runtime (lead: Priya) + SDK (Liam)
- KV controls: platform-engineering (Diego) + SRE
- Billing telemetry: observability + finance spike (owner: Maya)

Quick decision log (proposed, informal):
- Do probe 1 as first sprint (low friction, high customer perceptible impact).
- Run probe 2 as alpha with 2 customers after a security review.
- Probe 3 instrument-only in backend; hold UI until metrics show top 5 customers-only impact.

Notes to self / unresolved fragments:
- Need example API header name for sticky pin; suggestion: X-Redwood-Model-Pin: redwood-llm-x-quant-v1
- SDKs: check JavaScript reconnect semantics for streaming (track duplicate token de-dup logic)
- Can we emit "fallback_reason" in response header (e.g., capacity|latency|policy)? Cheap diagnostic.

Immediate action items (next 7 days):
- [Maya] Draft PRD-lite for session-sticky header + response-fallback header. Link to this doc.
- [Priya] Confirm routing trace availability and feasible tracing fields.
- [Liam] Patch JS SDK to expose fallback headers and test reconnect dedupe.
- [Diego] Spec tenant-KV-control auth model and short security checklist.

Appendix: quick tickets & links
- JIRA: JIRA-CS-1283 (billing-spike-investigation), ENG-DEV-2345 (routing-trace-add), SRE-789 (kv-evict-api-prototype)
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/staccato-voices-notes

End — informal scratch. Will prune and convert into CS playbook if probes get greenlit.
summary: Working notebook of short vignettes, prioritized low-effort probes, open questions and immediate owners to address runtime & billing feedback from customers. Emphasis on model-fallback visibility, KV-cache controls, and per-route billing telemetry.
